tossups.p: Coccolithophores, microscopic marine algae, are the main biological source of a soft, fine-grained variety of this rock that forms the White Cliffs of Dover. This rock lacks the magnesium found in the closely related rock dolomite.
tossups.r: Heat and pressure can metamorphose this rock into the smoother stone marble. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock made mostly of calcium carbonate.

tossups.p: Germany’s Solnhofen Lagerstätte, a famous formation of this rock, preserved nearly every detailed fossil scientists have of Archaeopteryx, one of the earliest known birds. This rock’s dissolution over time forms dramatic landscapes called karst topography, complete with sinkholes and winding caves.
tossups.r: Dripping water inside those caves slowly builds stalactites and stalagmites out of this rock. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock made up of the minerals aragonite and calcite.

tossups.p: Round grains called ooids, cemented together into a texture called oolite, form one variety of this rock, which also includes a loosely cemented, shell-fragment variety called coquina. This rock dissolves easily in weakly acidic rainwater, a process that can open up water-filled sinkholes called cenotes.
tossups.r: Egyptian builders cased the Great Pyramids of Giza in polished blocks of this rock. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock, the main ingredient in cement.

tossups.p: Mineral-rich water dripping and flowing through caves carved from this rock builds formations called speleothems, including flowstones. A fine-grained, spring-deposited variety of this rock can also form in porous, lightweight layers near waterfalls and streams.
tossups.r: Heating this rock in a kiln drives off carbon dioxide gas and leaves behind quicklime, used in farming and steelmaking. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock made mostly of calcium carbonate.

tossups.p: The crushed shells and skeletons of ancient marine creatures, piled up on old sea floors, formed much of this rock over millions of years. This rock is mostly made of the minerals aragonite and calcite, both forms of calcium carbonate.
tossups.r: Carbonic acid in rainwater slowly dissolves this rock, carving out caves, sinkholes, and other karst landscapes. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock that metamorphoses into marble.

tossups.p: Famous cave systems like Mammoth Cave in Kentucky and Carlsbad Caverns in New Mexico are carved from thick beds of this rock. Acid rain slowly eats away at outdoor statues and buildings made from this rock and its harder metamorphic cousin, marble.
tossups.r: This rock fizzes when touched with a drop of weak acid, since it is made mostly of calcium carbonate. For 10 points, name this common sedimentary rock.

tossups.p: This rock’s softest, chalkiest variety is made mostly of fossilized shells from coccolithophores, tiny ocean algae, and forms the famous White Cliffs of Dover. A closely related sedimentary rock called dolomite looks almost identical but contains extra magnesium that this rock lacks.
tossups.r: Builders have prized this rock for construction and as the main ingredient in cement for thousands of years. For 10 points, name this rock that forms marble when exposed to heat and pressure.

tossups.p: Round grains called ooids build up in wave-tossed shallow water to form a textured variety of this rock called oolite. This rock’s dissolution can carve out water-filled sinkholes called cenotes, famous in Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula.
tossups.r: Dripping groundwater inside its caves slowly deposits stalactites and stalagmites made of this rock. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock, made mostly of calcium carbonate.

tossups.p: A variety of this rock called coquina forms from loosely cemented fragments of shells and coral, while a spring-deposited variety forms in banded, layered sheets near mineral springs. This rock undergoes metamorphosis under heat and pressure to form the harder rock marble.
tossups.r: This rock is mostly composed of aragonite and calcite, two mineral forms of calcium carbonate. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock, which dissolves to form karst topography.

tossups.p: Ancient coral reefs, built by reef-forming corals that also secrete calcium carbonate, are a major biological source of this rock. This rock is mostly made of the minerals aragonite and calcite, unlike the closely related rock dolomite, which also contains magnesium.
tossups.r: Dripping water inside caves carved from this rock slowly builds stalactites and stalagmites. For 10 points, name this common sedimentary rock, found in abundance along coastlines and ancient sea beds.

tossups.p: Builders have quarried this rock for thousands of years, using it in construction and as the key raw ingredient in Portland cement. Heating this rock in a hot kiln drives off carbon dioxide gas and produces quicklime.
tossups.r: This rock dissolves in weakly acidic rainwater, forming caves, sinkholes, and other karst landscapes. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock that turns into marble under heat and pressure.

tossups.p: This rock is too hard to scratch with a fingernail but easy to scratch with a steel knife, sitting around 3 on the Mohs hardness scale. Dolines and water-filled cenotes form where this rock slowly dissolves underground, and a loosely cemented, shell-fragment variety of it is called coquina.
tossups.r: This rock is mostly made of calcium carbonate from ancient marine life. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock that metamorphoses into marble under heat and pressure.

tossups.p: Egyptian builders cased the Great Pyramids of Giza in polished white blocks of this rock. Round grains called ooids cement together to form a granular variety of this rock called oolite, often found in shallow, wave-churned water.
tossups.r: Fossilized seashells and coral fragments cemented together form another variety of this rock. For 10 points, name this sedimentary rock made mostly of calcium carbonate.

tossups.p: This rock’s chemical formula, CaCO3, is shared with the mineral calcite, one of its two main building blocks alongside aragonite. The dissolution of this rock over time creates dramatic landscapes called karst topography.
tossups.r: Stalactites hanging from cave ceilings and stalagmites rising from cave floors are usually made of this rock, deposited drop by drop. For 10 points, name this common sedimentary rock.

tossups.p: This rock’s varieties include coquina, made of loosely cemented shell fragments, and a banded type deposited by mineral-rich springs. This rock reacts with and fizzes in weak acids, which is how geologists often identify it in the field.
tossups.r: Acid rain gradually damages outdoor statues and buildings carved from this rock or its metamorphic cousin, marble. For 10 points, name this common sedimentary rock made mostly of calcium carbonate.

Heat and pressure can metamorphose it into the smoother rock marble

A key building material, and the main ingredient in cement and concrete
Fizzes when a drop of weak acid, like vinegar or dilute hydrochloric acid, touches it
Often formed from the crushed shells and skeletons of marine creatures that piled up on ancient sea floors
Dripping water inside caves slowly builds stalactites and stalagmites from it
A variety deposited by mineral-rich hot springs and dripping groundwater is sometimes banded or layered
Mostly made of the minerals aragonite and calcite, both forms of calcium carbonate
Acid rain slowly eats away at outdoor statues and buildings made of it
Chalk, a soft, fine-grained variety made mostly of microscopic algae shells, forms famous white cliffs like those at Dover
One variety called coquina is made of loosely cemented shell fragments; a more porous, spring-deposited type is called tufa
Heating it in a kiln drives off carbon dioxide and produces quicklime, used in steelmaking and farming
Unlike the closely related rock dolomite, it lacks magnesium
Coccolithophores, microscopic ocean algae, are the main biological source of its softest variety, chalk
Germany’s Solnhofen Lagerstätte, a formation of this rock, preserved nearly every known fossil of the early bird Archaeopteryx
Round grains called ooids, cemented together, form a textured variety of it called oolite

Its chemical formula, CaCO3, is the same one chemists write for the mineral calcite

trap.title: Limestone, marble, or dolomite?
trap.body: Heat and pressure turn limestone into marble, so the two rocks share the same basic ingredient, calcium carbonate, and real tossups constantly mention marble as limestone’s metamorphosed form. A closely related sedimentary rock called dolomite looks almost the same but contains magnesium, which limestone lacks.
trap.fix: If the clue says “sedimentary,” “fossils,” “shells,” or “dissolves in weak acid” (fizzes), it wants limestone. If the clue says “metamorphic” or describes a harder, often white or veined stone used by sculptors, it wants marble instead.
trap.line: Real answer line: Limestone [prompt on calcium carbonate or CaCO3; accept travertine before read]

topics.name: Basalt
topics.kicker: Dark, fine-grained volcanic rock · Makes up most of the ocean floor
topics.briefing: Basalt is the dark, heavy rock that forms when runny lava cools quickly, too fast for big crystals to grow. It makes up most of the ocean floor, the islands of Hawaii and Iceland, and even the dark “seas” you can see on the Moon. When a thick flow cools slowly and evenly, it can crack into giant six-sided columns, like the roughly 40,000 columns of Northern Ireland’s Giant’s Causeway.
topics.answerHtml: Basalt (accept basaltic rock or lava, flood basalts, or pillow basalts; prompt on volcanic rock, igneous rock, or mafic rock; do not accept “gabbro”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Followers of the German geologist Abraham Gottlob Werner, called Neptunists, wrongly argued that this rock had settled out of a vast ancient ocean. Other geologists showed that it actually forms from lava, partly by tracing its outcrops in France’s Auvergne [“oh-VAIRN”] region back to long-extinct volcanoes.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this dark, fine-grained igneous rock that makes up most of the ocean floor.

tossups.p: The word “trap” in the names of giant, step-like piles of this rock comes from a Swedish word for “stairs.” Eruptions that built the Siberian Traps from this rock are linked to the end-Permian mass extinction, and India’s Deccan Traps erupted around the time the dinosaurs disappeared.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this dark volcanic rock that forms the six-sided columns of Northern Ireland’s Giant’s Causeway.

tossups.p: Felix Mendelssohn wrote his overture _The Hebrides_ after visiting Fingal’s Cave, a sea cave on the Scottish island of Staffa that is lined with columns of this rock. Such columns form when a thick lava flow cools and shrinks, cracking into mostly six-sided pillars.
tossups.r: Similar columns make up Northern Ireland’s Giant’s Causeway. For 10 points, name this dark igneous rock that makes up most of the oceanic crust.

tossups.p: Apollo astronauts brought back samples of this rock from the lunar maria [“MAR-ee-uh”], the dark plains that early astronomers thought were seas on the Moon. On Earth, it is the most common kind of volcanic rock, and Hawaii’s shield volcanoes erupt it as runny lava.
tossups.r: Its slowly cooled, coarse-grained cousin is called gabbro. For 10 points, name this dark, fine-grained rock that forms most of the ocean floor.

tossups.p: A medium-grained rock with the same chemistry as this one, called diabase or dolerite, often forms the sheet-like intrusions called dikes and sills. This mafic rock is rich in magnesium and iron, which give it a dark color.
tossups.r: It is made mostly of pyroxene and plagioclase feldspar. For 10 points, name this fine-grained volcanic rock that forms the oceanic crust and Hawaii’s lava flows.

tossups.p: When gas-bubble holes called vesicles in this rock are later filled in with minerals such as zeolites [“ZEE-uh-lites”], the filled pockets are called amygdules [“uh-MIG-dyoolz”]. Scoria, a very bubbly volcanic rock that builds many cinder cones, usually has this rock’s chemistry.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this dark, fine-grained igneous rock whose slowly cooled, coarse-grained cousin is gabbro.

tossups.p: In Irish legend, the giant Finn McCool built a path across the sea toward Scotland out of interlocking columns of this rock. Those mostly six-sided columns in County Antrim, numbering about 40,000, formed as a thick flow of lava slowly cooled, shrank, and cracked.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this dark volcanic rock that forms the famous columns of Northern Ireland’s Giant’s Causeway.

tossups.p: Millions of years ago, long cracks in the ground poured out lava that hardened into layer after layer of this rock across Washington, Oregon, and Idaho, forming the Columbia River Plateau. Such fissure eruptions can build huge regions of this rock called large igneous provinces.
tossups.r: Hawaii’s shield volcanoes also erupt it as runny lava. For 10 points, name this dark rock that makes up most of the ocean floor.

tossups.p: Geologists use the abbreviation MORB for samples of this rock collected along mid-ocean ridges, where its lava erupts underwater and cools almost instantly into rounded “pillows.” Iceland, which sits on top of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, is built mostly of this rock.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this dark igneous rock that makes up most of the oceanic crust.

tossups.p: Pyroxene and calcium-rich plagioclase, minerals that crystallize at high temperatures in Bowen’s reaction series, are the main ingredients of this rock. Because this rock’s lava is low in silica, it flows easily and usually erupts gently instead of exploding.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this dark, fine-grained rock that builds Hawaii’s shield volcanoes and the ocean floor.

tossups.p: Melted and spun into thin fibers, this rock is used to make fire-resistant rock wool insulation. Crushed pieces of this hard, heavy rock are commonly used to build roads and to hold railroad tracks in place.
tossups.r: Its coarse-grained equivalent is gabbro. For 10 points, name this extrusive igneous rock that forms Hawaii’s volcanoes and most of the ocean floor.

tossups.p: Because this rock is denser than granite, oceanic crust made of it sinks beneath the lighter continents at subduction zones. New crust made of this rock forms constantly where tectonic plates pull apart along mid-ocean ridges.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this dark, fine-grained igneous rock whose slowly cooled, coarse-grained cousin is gabbro.

tossups.p: Soviet Venera landers found this rock on the surface of Venus, and it also covers much of Mars, where giant shield volcanoes like Olympus Mons erupted it as lava. On Earth, it erupts at hotspots like Hawaii and along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this dark volcanic rock that makes up most of the ocean floor.

tossups.p: Smooth, ropy pahoehoe [“pa-HOH-ay-HOH-ay”] and rough, jagged a‘a [“AH-ah”] are the two main kinds of lava flows made of this rock, named with Hawaiian words. Hawaii’s Mauna Loa and Kilauea [“kee-luh-WAY-uh”] are broad shield volcanoes built from its runny lava.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this dark, fine-grained volcanic rock that makes up most of the ocean floor.

tossups.p: This rock’s crystals are usually too small to see without a magnifying glass, because its lava cools quickly at Earth’s surface. Geologists call it extrusive, while gabbro, which has the same minerals but cooled slowly underground, is called intrusive.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this most common volcanic rock, a dark rock that forms the oceanic crust.

trap.title: Basalt or gabbro?
trap.body: Basalt and gabbro are made of the same minerals, so clues about pyroxene, plagioclase, or a mafic, iron-rich makeup fit both. The difference is where they cooled: basalt’s lava cooled fast at the surface, so its crystals are tiny, while gabbro’s magma cooled slowly underground into big crystals. Players also mix up basalt with granite, the light-colored, quartz-rich rock of the continents.
trap.fix: Fine-grained, extrusive, lava, the ocean floor, Hawaii, pillows, or the Giant’s Causeway means basalt. Coarse-grained, intrusive, or “cooled slowly underground” means gabbro. Light-colored, quartz, and continental crust mean granite, and natural volcanic glass means obsidian.
trap.line: Real answer line: Basalt (accept flood basalt or pillow basalt; prompt on volcanic rock or igneous rock; do not accept “gabbro”)

topics.name: Soil
topics.kicker: Mix of weathered rock, humus, water, and air · Where plants take root
topics.dates: Celebrated on World Soil Day, December 5
topics.briefing: Soil is the loose layer of crumbled rock, decayed plants and animals, water, and air that covers much of Earth’s land. A single handful can hold billions of microbes, and almost all of our food grows in it. Dig down and you’ll find layers called horizons: dark, humus-rich topsoil near the surface, then subsoil, then broken-up rock, and finally solid bedrock.
topics.answerHtml: Soil (accept soils or pedosphere; prompt on dirt, earth, ground, regolith, or topsoil; do not accept a lower layer like “subsoil” or “bedrock” or one particle size like “sand,” “silt,” or “clay”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Vasily Dokuchaev [“duh-koo-CHAH-yef”], often called the founder of the science that studies this material, wrote a famous study of the Russian steppe’s chernozem [“chair-nuh-ZYAWM”], whose name means “black earth.” Scientists who study this material are called pedologists.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this mixture of weathered rock, decayed organic matter, water, and air in which plants grow.

tossups.p: Hans Jenny’s equation for the five factors that form this material is remembered by the acronym CLORPT: climate, organisms, relief, parent material, and time. Its A horizon, near the surface, is usually darkened by decayed organic matter called humus.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this loose layer of sand, silt, clay, and humus that covers much of Earth’s land.

tossups.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture sorts this material into twelve orders with names ending in “-sol,” such as Mollisols, which form under grasslands, and Oxisols [“OX-ih-sawlz”], which are often red from iron in the tropics. A balanced mix of particle sizes in this material is called loam.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this material whose particles, from largest to smallest, are sand, silt, and clay.

tossups.p: Charles Darwin’s final book described how earthworms slowly build up the top layer of this material by passing it through their bodies. Bits of decayed plants and animals in this material break down into a dark substance called humus.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this mixture of weathered rock, organic matter, water, and air that covers much of Earth’s land.

tossups.p: Streptomyces [“strep-toh-MY-seez”] bacteria in this material make geosmin [“jee-OZ-min”], a chemical behind the earthy smell after a rain. Selman Waksman’s lab found the antibiotic streptomycin in a kind of bacteria that commonly lives in this material.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this material whose layers are called horizons and whose particles include sand, silt, and clay.

tossups.p: Scientists describe the color of this material by matching it to Munsell charts, and they classify its texture on a triangle-shaped diagram. That diagram’s three sides show the percentages of three particle sizes in a sample of this material.
tossups.r: Those particles are sand, silt, and clay, and a balanced mix of them is called loam. For 10 points, name this material in which plants take root.

tossups.p: Hugh Hammond Bennett led a new federal agency created during the Dust Bowl of the 1930s to protect this resource, which strong winds were stripping from Great Plains farms. Farmers fight erosion of this resource with contour plowing, terraces, cover crops, and rows of trees called windbreaks.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this resource, a mixture of weathered rock and humus in which crops grow.

tossups.p: A pedon [“PED-ahn”] is the smallest three-dimensional unit of this material that scientists sample, and its natural clumps are called peds. Its layers, called horizons, run from an O horizon of fallen leaves down toward solid bedrock.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this layer of weathered rock and organic matter in which plants grow.

tossups.p: Red, iron-rich laterite [“LAT-uh-rite”] is a kind of this material found in hot, rainy places, and its name comes from the Latin word for “brick.” Heavy rain can carry nutrients down and out of this material in a process called leaching.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this material whose texture depends on its mix of sand, silt, and clay.

tossups.p: Some hydrangea flowers turn blue when this material is acidic and pink when it is alkaline, and gardeners spread lime on it to raise its pH. Earthworms tunneling through this material let in air and water.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this mixture of minerals, humus, water, and air that covers most of Earth’s land.

tossups.p: Ancient peoples in the Amazon mixed charcoal and food waste into the ground, creating terra preta [“TEH-ruh PRAY-tuh”], a dark and unusually fertile kind of this material. In deserts, a hard, cement-like layer called caliche [“kuh-LEE-chee”] can form inside it.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this material in which plants grow, whose layers are called horizons.

tossups.p: Minerals washed out of this material’s E horizon by eluviation [“ih-loo-vee-AY-shun”] build up lower down in its B horizon, a zone of accumulation. Above them, its O horizon is made of fallen leaves and other organic matter.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this mixture of weathered rock, humus, water, and air in which plants grow.

tossups.p: Deep, fertile examples of this material in the American Midwest and northern China developed from loess [“LOH-ess”], thick deposits of wind-blown silt. Clay-rich Vertisols are a kind of this material that swells when wet and cracks deeply when dry.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this material that farmers plow, made of weathered rock, humus, water, and air.

tossups.p: The rhizosphere [“RY-zoh-sfeer”] is the thin zone of this material right around a plant’s roots, teeming with bacteria and fungi. Some bacteria living in this material turn nitrogen gas from the air into compounds that plants can use.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this material whose particles are sand, silt, and clay, mixed with decayed organic matter called humus.

tossups.p: The United Nations honors this material every December 5, and it named 2015 an international year dedicated to it. Some scientists call it Earth’s “living skin,” and a single handful can hold billions of microbes.
tossups.r: Its layers are called horizons. For 10 points, name this mixture of weathered rock, humus, water, and air in which plants grow.

clues.t: A loose mixture of weathered rock bits, decayed organic matter, water, and air that covers much of Earth’s land
Plants take root in it, and nearly all of our crops grow in it
Its layers are called horizons; a slice showing all of them is called a profile
Its mineral particles, from largest to smallest, are sand, silt, and clay
A balanced mix of sand, silt, and clay is called loam, great for growing crops
Humus is the dark, decayed plant and animal matter in it
From the top down: O (leaf litter), A (dark and humus-rich), E, B (zone of accumulation), C (broken rock), and R (bedrock)
Its scientific study is called pedology, and the scientists are called pedologists
Strong winds stripped it from Great Plains farms in the 1930s Dust Bowl; Hugh Hammond Bennett led a new federal agency to protect it
Farmers fight its erosion with contour plowing, terraces, cover crops, and windbreaks
Leaching: rainwater carries dissolved nutrients down and out of it
Earthworms tunnel through it, mixing it and letting in air and water
Some hydrangeas bloom blue in acidic examples and pink in alkaline ones; spreading lime raises its pH
Its texture is classified on a triangle diagram showing the percentages of sand, silt, and clay
Vasily Dokuchaev, often called the founder of its science, studied the chernozem (“black earth”) of the Russian steppe
Hans Jenny’s CLORPT: climate, organisms, relief, parent material, and time are the factors that form it
The USDA sorts it into twelve orders ending in “-sol,” like grassland Mollisols and red tropical Oxisols
Charles Darwin’s final book (1881) showed how earthworms slowly build up its top layer
Streptomyces bacteria in it make geosmin, part of the earthy smell after rain; the antibiotic streptomycin came from one of these bacteria
Its color is described by matching it to Munsell color charts
A pedon is its smallest sampled three-dimensional unit; its natural clumps are called peds
Laterite: a red, iron-rich tropical kind, named from the Latin for “brick”
Terra preta: a dark, fertile Amazon kind made by ancient peoples who mixed in charcoal
Eluviation washes minerals out of the E horizon; illuviation deposits them in the B horizon
Caliche: a hard, cement-like layer of calcium carbonate that forms in desert examples
Fertile Midwest and Chinese examples developed from loess (wind-blown silt); clay-rich Vertisols swell and crack
The rhizosphere is the zone right around plant roots, teeming with microbes; some bacteria there fix nitrogen
The United Nations honors it every December 5, and 2015 was its international year

trap.title: A part isn’t the whole
trap.body: Tossups on this answer are full of its ingredients and layers: sand, silt, clay, humus, loam, subsoil, and bedrock. Buzzing with one of those parts is wrong, because the question wants the whole material. Players who say “dirt” or “earth” will usually be asked to be more specific, and “topsoil,” which is only the top layer, earns a prompt too.
trap.fix: When a clue lists particles (sand, silt, clay), layers (horizons, the A horizon, bedrock), or kinds (loam, laterite, chernozem), answer with the whole material: soil. Save “sand” or “clay” for a question that asks for one particle size. If you are prompted after saying “topsoil,” just say “soil.”
trap.line: Real answer line: Soil (accept pedosphere; prompt on dirt, earth, or topsoil; do not accept “sand,” “silt,” “clay,” or “subsoil”)
